sermon.title: Jesus' Processing Plan, Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Jesus’ Processing Plan, Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer says no one takes the honor of a calling to himself; God places people in the body as he sees fit, and the apostles were given authority and understanding by Jesus. He explains from his own experience why he moved away from personal prophecy to “a more excellent way,” love, and says all believers can worship, love and ask God for wisdom.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: At 8:23 he cites “First Corinthians 12 … 29” (the words between are unclear in the captions); the verse he reads, “Are all apostles?”, is 1 Corinthians 12:29. Some passages he quotes without naming the reference (e.g. Proverbs 10:19, 1 John 4:7, Acts 11 on Antioch and Agabus); the references are added here for the reader.

faqs.question: Do you have to be a preacher to win people to Christ?
faqs.answer: He tells of a woman who won multitudes to Christ by baking cakes for neighbors and talking to them about Jesus; she was not a preacher, apostle or prophet. He says we are the followers and the responders.

faqs.question: Is it wrong to write notes in your Bible?
faqs.answer: He says some think it is sacrilegious, but it is just a book with a living word in it and he needs every help he can get. He wrote down what God revealed so he could go back and share it later.

faqs.question: What does passing Jesus’ processing plan produce?
faqs.answer: He says the apostles passed the processing plan, so nothing could move or sway them, and you never read of them running off with the church’s money or having a breakdown. He says we may not be apostles or prophets, but we can be unstoppable, unmovable and unchangeable in our walk with God.

faqs.question: What is “the testimony of Jesus” in Revelation 19:10?
faqs.answer: He says the testimony of Jesus, the witness and proof of Jesus, is the spirit of prophecy, and that it should be operating in the church.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And I fell at his feet to worship him. But he said to me, “See that you do not do that! I am your fellow servant, and of your brethren who have the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”

faqs.question: What does the example of Agabus show about prophets?
faqs.answer: He says Agabus could prophesy the famine coming and it happened, so the church could prepare relief, and that kind of office is rare.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then one of them, named Agabus, stood up and showed by the Spirit that there was going to be a great famine throughout all the world, which also happened in the days of Claudius Caesar. Then the disciples, each according to his ability, determined to send relief to the brethren dwelling in Judea.

faqs.question: Should believers wait for great men of God to spread the gospel?
faqs.answer: He says no; the church at Antioch was established by believers before the apostles came, and God will back us up as we preach the gospel. He says each person has a tremendous destiny if they respond to his processing plan.

faqs.question: How should you thank someone after a good message?
faqs.answer: He likes “thank you for letting God use you,” because a message is not great unless God gives it; the man does not get the credit, any more than the donkey that spoke to Balaam.

faqs.question: If a prophecy does not come to pass, did the prophet miss?
faqs.answer: He says that when a person fails to respond to a prophecy it seems the prophet missed, when in reality the receiver failed to respond.

faqs.question: Why does he call love the high calling of God?
faqs.answer: He says God is love, so we need to spend time with him and take on his nature; without love he is just going through motions. He calls love the high calling of God.

faqs.question: Does wisdom matter at home?
faqs.answer: He says it works on the local level: wives want wise husbands, husbands wise wives, parents wise children. He says God gives it liberally, but we do not spend time asking for it.

scriptures.text_nkjv: If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.

faqs.question: Should the church hide behind the Lord’s return?
faqs.answer: He says the church should not be hiding behind a return wanting to get out of this, but pushing in to be a force in the earth to bring peace on the earth.
